newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends up on year end book squaring.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends up on year end book squaring.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended higher Tuesday on light volumes, driven by year-end position squaring.
COMEX will be closed for the New Year holiday Wednesday.
"There was almost nobody in the market today, leaving just some book squaring to be done, which meant the offer got chased back up," one trader said.
COMEX March copper ended up 2.00 cents at 100.25 cents a pound, after seeing a session high at 100.30 cents.
Total estimated volume was only 3,500 lots.
The COMEX January/March spread ended little changed at 2.60 cents.
Earlier LME three month copper ended little changed, despite a further rise in LME warehouse copper stocks.
LME stocks rose 3,950 tonnes to 125,350 tonnes. COMEX stocks were up 1,169 short tons Monday to 30,519 short tons.
In the past month, both COMEX and LME copper have been drifting back from six month highs, as LME stocks have recovered from six year lows.
"We are becoming much less bearish about the short term outlook for copper prices," Merill Lynch analyst Ted Arnold said.

"Chinese demand combined with normal growth in the rest of the world is likely to consume almost all of the extra copper coming on stream with the result that we are unlikely to see much of a suppl surplus develop," he said.
